items.stem: What does a branch protection rule requiring pull request reviews primarily prevent?

options.text: Unreviewed changes being merged directly into a protected branch
options.rationale: Correct: it forces changes through review before they reach the protected branch.

options.text: All commits to any branch in the repository
options.rationale: It targets the protected branch, not every branch.
Protection rules govern merges, not cloning.
Protection rules do not disable Actions.

items.explanation: Correct: it forces changes through review before they reach the protected branch.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices for secrets in GitHub Actions? (Select TWO)

options.text: Store tokens as encrypted repository or environment secrets
options.rationale: Correct: secrets are encrypted and injected at runtime, not stored in source.

options.text: Reference secrets via the secrets context in the workflow
options.rationale: Correct: workflows read them through the secrets context rather than literals.

options.text: Commit the token directly in the workflow YAML for convenience
options.rationale: Hardcoding secrets exposes them in history.

options.text: Print the secret to the log to confirm it loaded
options.rationale: Logging secrets leaks them; Actions masks but you must not print them.

items.explanation: Correct: secrets are encrypted and injected at runtime, not stored in source.

items.stem: Which statement best distinguishes Git from GitHub?

options.text: Git is the version-control tool; GitHub is a hosting and collaboration platform built around it
options.rationale: Correct: Git tracks versions locally; GitHub hosts repositories and adds collaboration features.

options.text: GitHub is the version-control tool and Git is the website
They are two names for the same program
options.rationale: They are distinct: a tool and a platform.

options.text: Git only works if GitHub is online
options.rationale: Git works fully offline without GitHub.

items.explanation: Correct: Git tracks versions locally; GitHub hosts repositories and adds collaboration features.
